messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty INC-2026-4729 triggered for service= inference-gateway — 5xx error rate spike detected (5m avg=6.8%, baseline=0.3%). Region=us-east1. Links: https://pd.redwood/inci/INC-2026-4729 and http://grafana.redwood/d/inference/5xx-rate

pagerduty: Auto-page: Escalation policy = SRE-primary. Page sent to rotation.

alice: acked. taking first look. can someone check whether this aligns with the canary push that landed ~18:05? :eyes:

ben-sre: on it. i'm pulling logs now. if it's timeouts we might be hitting worker kv-cache evictions again.

carla-eng: i saw a small rollout at 18:02 — a routing change that pins some traffic to model-v3-quant. not sure if it's related. forwarding deploy link: https://deploys/redwood/job/rollout/4987

ekaterina-sre: quick check — gateway latency p50 up from 28ms -> 220ms, p95 1.2s -> 3.8s. 5xx composition is mostly 502/504 (upstream reset & timeout).

dylan-release: if it's the canary, we can abort/rollback the routing. want me to hold traffic back to stable?

alice: yes hold. ben, can you confirm backend pool health first?

ben-sre: running queries against logs. sample error stream: ```[2026-04-12T18:07:14Z] inference-gateway ERROR backend: connection reset by peer (multi)
[2026-04-12T18:07:15Z] inference-gateway WARN request latency exceeded 3s, upstream=worker-57
[2026-04-12T18:07:16Z] inference-gateway ERROR 502 response from /v1/complete model=model-v3-quant```

ben-sre: kibana query: `service:inference-gateway AND status:[500 TO 599] AND @timestamp:now-10m` — trending spikes coincide with canary roll.

carla-eng: rolling back the model routing now. running `rctl rollout abort --job=4987` then `rctl route set inference-gateway --slice=canary --weight=0`

dylan-release: i'm ready to push the rollback if we want immediate cut. approve?

alice: yes please. do it, and keep canary pods up for postmortem.

pagerduty: Reminder: If there is customer impact escalate to Severity=SEV2.

ekaterina-sre: current customer-facing error surface: about ~1.2% of user requests getting 5xx in us-east1 (traffic-weighted). Some customers on stable traffic reported request errors in the last 10m via support. i'd mark user-visible errors as intermittent but visible.

night-oncall: i'm here, taking the night handoff once we have stabilization. please ping me when the rate returns to baseline.

carla-eng: rollback command executed at 18:10:03Z. canary weight -> 0. routing change propagated to edge 18:10:25Z.

ben-sre: watching metrics — error rate trending down. 5m avg now 3.2% -> 1.0% in last 3m.

alice: running a targeted health check against affected endpoints:```curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://inference-gateway.us-east1.redwood.internal/v1/complete -d '{"prompt":"test"}' | jq .``` returns 200 for sampled requests.

ben-sre: also restarted a couple of worker pods that showed repeated connection resets: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/model-worker-quant --namespace=prod-us-east1` (done 18:12Z).

dylan-release: i'm leaving the aborted canary in the deploy UI for the postmortem; no new traffic to model-v3-quant.

ekaterina-sre: PD note: keeping this as SEV2 due to customer-visible errors and partial region impact. Slack notifications to account owners triggered.

pagerduty: Pager acknowledged by alice at 18:08:01Z. Escalated to ben-sre at 18:08:45Z.

carla-eng: logs show a surge of backend connection refused from worker group model-v3-quant between 18:05-18:11, likely due to an incompatible quantized kernel causing OOM/backpressure. i'm filing a ticket on the model onboarding side.

alice: can someone sanity-check cost/scale implications if we need to temporarily route more to stable? don't want to blow through reserved limits.

ben-sre: temporary shift should be fine within burst policy — checked reserved pool headroom for us-east1; we have ~25% slack. i'll keep an eye.

night-oncall: confirmed received handoff. i'll be monitoring dashboards and pinging oncall-sre if anything regresses.

ben-sre: 18:18Z metrics: 5xx 5m avg = 0.9%, last 1m = 0.6%. p95 latency back to 240ms. looks stable.

dylan-release: marking rollback as successful in deploy UI. tagging the rollout with `auto-rollback:pd-INC-2026-4729`.

alice: thanks all. i'll open the incident ticket and start timeline for postmortem: root cause suspected = canary model variant triggered worker instability (quant kernel OOM/backpressure). next steps: revert model onboarding until compatibility checks added, add a canary traffic ramp guard.

carla-eng: adding immediate mitigations to runbook: 1) stricter canary traffic ramp (max 5% over 10m), 2) autopage-silence on known noisy deploys, 3) add worker OOM alert thresholds.

pagerduty: Incident INC-2026-4729 auto-ack closed by alice at 18:24:59Z after stabilization.

ekaterina-sre: final check: no lingering elevated errors in other regions, marking incident as resolved for now. will coordinate the postmortem doc in #postmortems. :white_check_mark:
